title: Constraint-driven Prompt Orchestrator — sandbox notes
content:
Quick brain-dump: idea vault for a small product experiment — 'Constraint-driven Prompt Orchestrator' (CDPO). Rough notes, use as a personal sandbox rather than a polished PRD.

Context / problem:
- Many apps need to compose signals (policy constraints, user preferences, token budgets, persona guidelines, data redaction rules) into a final request to the model.
- Current flow is brittle: either the client composes a single monolithic prompt (hard to reason about or mutate at runtime), or server-side we apply ad-hoc string ops that get messy when we add new constraints.
- We also want to switch constraints at inference time (e.g., degrade persona fidelity to stay within a token SLO, or enforce a legal redaction step for regulated customers).
- Need: an engine to declaratively combine modular prompt fragments, apply deterministic constraints, and resolve tradeoffs (cost vs. fidelity) at request time.

Goals (stretch & success metrics):
- Experiment: prototype a tiny orchestrator that composes 3 fragment types (system directives, user-supplied input, constraint filters) and outputs a final prompt + metadata.
- Latency budget: orchestration step < 8ms in-hosted flow (in-path), ideally non-blocking for streaming start.
- Cost guardrail: able to specify a per-request token budget and choose between compression strategies (summaries, truncation, compression LLM) to meet it.
- Developer ergonomics: API surface should allow toggling constraints without changing prompt text.
- Metrics: percent of requests requiring on-the-fly compression, average tokens saved, downstream quality delta (eval set).

Key concepts / primitives:
- Fragment: named block with type {system, persona, tool-instruction, safety-filter, summary, user}. Carries a priority integer and an optional 'mutate' flag.
- Constraint: rule object (string for now) e.g., "max_tokens: 512", "redact: PII,SSN". Later map to structured checks.
- Resolver: function that takes fragments + constraints + request signals and returns: {final_prompt, applied_fragments, decisions}. Decisions include why a fragment was dropped or compressed (reason code).
- Strategy profiles: pre-canned resolution strategies (aggressive-compress, preserve-persona, low-latency) that influence the resolver.

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I want to enable 'strict-privacy' mode for a customer so that any fragment flagged as 'sensitive' is removed or replaced with a safe summary before sending to the model.
- As an SRE, I want to set a global token SLO per route that triggers compression strategies if request estimated tokens > SLO to avoid p95 latency regressions.
- As an ML engineer, I want to run A/B between 'compress-with-summary-llm' vs 'truncate-context' on a representative prompt set and measure quality delta.

Proposed MVP behaviors (keep small):
- API: POST /orchestrate with body {fragments: [{name,type,content,priority,meta}], constraints: [{key,value}], strategy: "preserve-persona"} returns {prompt, tokens_estimate, decisions}.
- Built-in strategies: preserve-persona (keep system + persona fragments, compress user fragments), cost-first (compress earliest fragments until budget), strict-redact (remove fragments tagged sensitive).
- Compression primitives: naive truncation (token-based), extractive summarization (few-shot LLM call, optional), local heuristics (remove low-priority bullets). Only implement truncation + extractive summary via hosted quick-call for MVP.
- Decision logging: for each request produce a terse decision vector (list of kept/dropped/summarized fragment ids and reason codes). Persist small sample to optimize policies.

Integration surface with Redwood platform:
- Hosted API: inline orchestrator as middleware on route (configurable per-route in console). Option to offload heavy compression to async pre-processor.
- Dedicated/Private: provide a library (python/ts) that runs same resolution logic locally so customers can run orchestration inside VPC.
- Console: enable 'strategy overrides' per route, visualize applied decisions for sample requests.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- End-to-end flow that composes 3 fragments and applies at least 2 strategies.
- Unit tests for resolver deterministic behavior given seed scenarios.
- Basic telemetry emits decisions with tag "orchestrator.v1".
- Small A/B harness to compare quality on 200 prompts (we track accept/reject by heuristic or human).

Open questions / risks:
- Security: summarization step calls LLM -> may reintroduce PII. Need to gate summarization for customers with strict regulation. Option: local summarizer (ffwd) or block.
- Latency tradeoffs: calling LLM to compress increases tail. Might need async prewarm or cached summaries.
- Complexity of priority collision: what if two high-priority fragments contradict? Need deterministic merge rules (higher priority wins; tie-breaker: fragment created_at).
- Operator UX: how to expose fragment templates in console without making it painful (templating language?).
- Evaluation: how to measure subtle quality changes when fragments are compressed. Human eval vs heuristics.

Mini experiments to run (order of priority):
1) Synthetic bench: implement resolver that does truncation + simple extractive summary via a small LLM call. Create 500 synthetic fragment sets with known ground-truth answers. Measure latency and quality (exact match heuristics).
2) Feature-flag in hosted API for a small customer cohort. Route sample requests through orchestrator and record decisions & token delta. 2-week pilot.
3) Local CLI tool: expose a single-file python resolver so SRE/product can iterate without deploying.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Draft a Linear ticket list: INF-4721 (MVP impl), INF-4722 (console UI), INF-4723 (telemetry & sampling).
- Talk to Nina about privacy guardrails — ask whether summarization is allowed by default for private customers.
- Prototype decision format (short list of codes) and sample event schema for tracing.
- Quick UX sketch for console: small toggle per route + 'debug sample' viewer that shows original fragments vs final prompt.

Potential future directions (post-MVP):
- Constraint algebra: allow boolean composition (AND/OR) of constraints to express complex rules.
- Fallback policy engine: route to smaller model variant when budget tight, or fall back to a cached canned response.
- Fragment library marketplace: curated reusable fragments (e.g., GDPR redaction, polite-tone) with templating.
- Local, on-device summarizer for stricter privacy regimes.

Random thoughts / heuristics we might like:
- Keep persona/system at >80% fidelity unless explicit strategy says otherwise.
- When compressing, prefer summarization of low-priority content over dropping high-priority structural bullets.
- Persist a lightweight fingerprint of the original prompt so we can compute regressions later without storing PII.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Wire up a tiny resolver in a sandbox repo (python script + simple API wrapper). Target: get a synthetic bench running by Friday.
- Sync with Nina and Samir for privacy and product constraints on Tuesday.
- Create Linear tickets and add 'orchestrator' tag to infra backlog.

End of notes. This doc will be iterated; it's a messy living scratchpad. Keep it here rather than in shared_drives until the concept crystalizes.
